audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Quinn level 3, first item and 2+ items, and gave Skill to levels 4-5 and 6, on a 53.01% Cho'Gath win rate. The whys say level 3 'trades skill out', levels 4-5 stabilise 'in my favor', level 6 'flips outright', and the late game is 'straight up I own the 1v1'. The difficulty label of TRICKY 7.5/10 also does not match a lane the text says you own from level 4 onward.
audit.why: Quinn has one window — levels 2-3, Harrier autos plus Vault mobility. After that Carnivore out-heals single-target poke and Feast is a true-damage execute against a marksman with no resistances who has to enter melee range to proc Harrier.
audit.corrected: Skill / Quinn / Skill / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath — the packet chart — as one atomic group across win[0..6] and phases[0..6].side+rating, plus diff EVEN and diffRating 6/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Phase text named Heartsteel as the spike and 'levels 2-3 (full pattern)' as Cho'Gath's window — levels 2-3 are the only window Quinn has.
audit.why: The spikes are Vault at 2 for her, level 6 for you, and every HP item afterwards, because her damage does not scale into an HP-stacking target and yours does.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions are absent from every field. (1) Vault 'briefly interrupt[s]' the target on impact, per Riot's own text — so Quinn can cancel a Feast cast by dashing into you, which is the single most expensive thing that can happen in this lane. (2) Blinding Assault blinds ('hinder its vision'), and Vorpal Spikes triggers off Cho'Gath's attacks — a blind therefore switches your E damage off entirely, not just your autos. Neither appears anywhere in either layer, though dontsFull[0].t vaguely says 'Fight into her blind'.
audit.why: The page tells the player to all-in at 6 without warning that her 12s E cancels the ultimate they are all-inning with, and it treats Blinding Assault as generic poke when it is the reason your damage output goes to zero for its duration.
audit.corrected: Vault's interrupt written into report[5].t, dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns; the blind's effect on Vorpal Spikes into tradeBad, dosFull[1].d and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns was placeholder text with no numbers.
audit.why: Vault at 12s rank 1 and Blinding Assault at 11s rank 1 are the two windows; Vault is the one worth baiting because it is both her escape and her interrupt.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every content why and all three prose blocks are written in the first person — 'I have one in Rupture', 'chip me', 'my Rupture cooldown', 'straight up I own the 1v1'.
audit.why: The rest of the site is second person. A page that switches to the coach's own voice mid-matchup reads as a different author.
audit.corrected: All seven whys converted to second person inside the length band. The early, mid and late blocks carry the same problem and still need a pass.

notes: The early, mid and late prose blocks are all written in the first person ('my Rupture', 'I take over', 'I own the 1v1'). I converted the seven whys inside the length band but could not rewrite three 400-500 character blocks into second person without exceeding +/-10% on at least one of them, so they still need a manual voice pass — this is a whole-matchup voice problem, not a fact problem. NOT ASSERTED: whether Vault's brief interrupt is long enough to cancel Feast specifically (Riot's text says 'briefly interrupting it' without naming what it interrupts, so I wrote the interrupt as a fact and the Feast risk as a consequence to respect, not as a tested certainty); whether Feral Scream can prevent Quinn ending Behind Enemy Lines early; and whether Blinding Assault's blind is cleansable. Quinn's R shows a 3s cooldown in Riot's data, which is the recast window rather than a real ultimate cooldown, so I quoted no number for it anywhere.
